design.protocol: leave-one-metal-out; Ru and Ir only, the two folds lomo_resolvability_audit calls resolvable
design.single_variable: protocol.pairwise_weight 0.0 (bce) vs 1.0 (pairwise); every other YAML key is identical
design.pairwise_loss: -log sigmoid((f(x+) - f(x-) - margin) / T) over every (active, inactive) pair in a batch, f = active-class logit

kill.rule: pairwise < 0.61 with the BCE arm reproduced closes the LOMO line

caveats: The first pairwise run fed the whole (B, 2) logit vector into the term and scored 0.4377. That run is a bug, not an arm: pushing both class scores apart fights the classifier. The shipped term takes column 1.
Two metals, five seeds. The per-metal split (Ru 0.6191, Ir 0.5665) moves in opposite directions, so the mean is not evidence that the term is neutral for every fold.
The term pairs every active row with every inactive row in the batch, not within (ligand, cell) groups as UP-24 did. That is a different pairing rule and the two deltas are not directly comparable.
margin and temperature are at their neutral values (0.0 / 1.0); no sweep was run, so this is one point in that space, not a best case.

The BCE arm lands at 0.5924 against the 0.5974 the resolvability audit reports. The 0.005 gap is inside the frozen tolerance but is not zero; the audit aggregated a stored artifact while this arm retrained.
